title: Merge the caputils/ and capchild/ directories

notes.body:
caputils is a library that combines 1) code that wraps libpcap/WinPcap/Npcap and covers up differences between:

1. the way we link with them (directly on UN\*X, via run-time loading of wpcap.dll on Windows, due to libpcap being a built-in library on UN\*Xes and an add-on for Windows);
1. having to work with different versions of libpcap/WinPcap/Npcap with different capabilities (older versions don't have all the APIs that we can use)

and 2) code to handle things currently *not* handled by libpcap/WinPcap/Npcap and that are done differently on different platforms, and thus having to do platform-dependent stuff such as getting "list of interfaces on this machine changed" notifications and controlling the Wi-Fi channel on which to capture.

capchild is a library for running dumpcap and communicating with it to do various capture-related functions.  The code in capchild/capture_ifinfo.c does that, so it's in the proper location.

However, `capture_interface_list()`, as it currently exists, is a bit of an ugly hack.

It's called from four places:

1. dumpcap;
1. the ui library;
1. capture_opts.c;
1. TShark.

There are *two* implementations of `capture_interface_list()`.

One is in dumpcap, which, obviously, operates by directly calling \*pcap ("obviously" as in "it obviously can't run dumpcap to do it"...).

The *other* is the one in capchild, which is used by all *other* programs.

If you have direct access to libpcap - i.e., if you're running inside dumpcap - you should get the interface list by itself.

Otherwise, you should get it by running dumpcap and reading the results from dumpcap.

*Currently*, that's done by having two versions of `capture_interface_list()`, with the same API - one inside dumpcap, which is linked with caputils, and one in capchild, for use by programs that run dumpcap to do the work.

The problem is that some of the routines that call `capture_interface_list()` are used both in dumpcap and in programs that run dumpcap to get the interface information, which is why we have the two-implementations hack.

Perhaps that should be done with a function pointer passed to those routines, instead.
Should "capture_ifinfo.h" be moved to capchild/ instead?

> Should "capture_ifinfo.h" be moved to capchild/ instead?

It could be, or it could be put in the top-level directory.  It's a bit weird, in that it's an interface not really exported by any single piece of code, but that's *imported* by several independent bits of code.

I think that's the universe's way of tell us that it should be done differently.

(Note also that capture_opts.[ch] is another set of code that probably should find a home in some library.)
I suggest putting all the files in caputils and capchild in the top-level directory, but keep the CMake target (library). Is that OK for you?

commits_data.title: Merge the caputils/ and capchild/ directories
commits_data.message:
Merge the caputils/ and capchild/ directories

The distinction between the different kinds of capture utility
may not warrant a special subfolfer for each, and sometimes the
distinction is not be clear or some functions could stradle
multiple "categories" (like capture_ifinfo.[ch]).

Simplify by having only a generic 'capture' subfolder. The
separate CMake libraries are kept as a way to reuse object code
efficiently.
